```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The paper's real-data task predicts an exporter's 2019 trade-outcome tensor
using 2018 trade and covariates. This vignette covers three distinct steps:
obtain the official sources, rebuild and check the analysis inputs, and fit
the authors' RGD/RGN methods. The runnable package example at the end uses
synthetic data; building this vignette neither downloads trade data nor runs
the long experiment. Raw and processed trade values are **not distributed**.
To run the real-data steps, obtain the **source checkout** of `SegreCP`, which
contains `reproducibility/real_data/`; that directory is excluded from the
installed R package and its source tarball.

The fixed paper design has 80 exporters, six covariates, a `25 x 21 x 8`
response tensor per exporter, CP rank three, and five common folds of 16
exporters. The covariates summarize tariffs, logistics, partner GDP, distance,
trade-agreement scope, and world demand. Exporter ranking and trade-exposure
weights use 2018 trade; 2019 trade values supply the response. Within each
fold, feature standardization and response-channel centering are estimated
using training exporters only.

The registered preprocessing uses three-level agreement scope,
square-root trade-value weights, untransformed tariffs, mean/standard-deviation
feature scaling, and centered (not variance-scaled) responses. The historical
reporter-candidate screen also requires 2019 WITS tariff availability,
2018--2019 WDI completeness, and 2018--2019 Gravity coverage. Consequently,
the selected sample is **not** a strictly 2018-information-only prospective
design, although the screen does not inspect 2019 trade outcomes. The WITS
availability filter excluded KOR and MEX in the frozen selection.

## Official sources

The download and parsing scripts under `reproducibility/real_data/` in the
package **source checkout** record the exact requests and validate their
responses. The upstream routes are:

| Input | Pinned source route | Analysis use |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Trade values and quantities | [CEPII BACI HS17 V202601 archive](https://www.cepii.fr/DATA_DOWNLOAD/baci/data/BACI_HS17_V202601.zip) ([catalogue](https://www.cepii.fr/CEPII/en/bdd_modele/bdd_modele_item.asp?id=37)) | 2018 sample selection and exposure weights; 2019 outcomes |
| Bilateral covariates | [CEPII Gravity V202211 archive](https://www.cepii.fr/DATA_DOWNLOAD/gravity/data/Gravity_rds_V202211.zip) ([catalogue](https://www.cepii.fr/CEPII/en/bdd_modele/bdd_modele_item.asp?id=8)) | 2018 distance and agreement scope |
| GDP and population | [World Bank WDI API](https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD?date=2018:2019&format=json&per_page=20000) | 2018 market-size inputs |
| Logistics | [World Bank LPI API](https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/LP.LPI.OVRL.XQ?date=2018&format=json&per_page=20000) | 2018 logistics proxy |
| MFN tariffs | [WITS/UNCTAD TRAINS API](https://wits.worldbank.org/) | 2018 importer-by-section tariffs |

The two Gravity files checked by the workflow are the official
`Gravity_rds_V202211.zip` archive and its extracted
`Gravity_V202211.rds` member, not two independent datasets. Their exact sizes
and SHA-256 values are pinned in `reference_source_manifest_sha256.csv`.

The WDI script also requests GDP per capita and population. The WITS script
resolves reporter codes and obtains the `reported` or `aveestimated` schedule
specified by official availability metadata. The exact reporter URLs and
source SHA-256 values are recorded in the local download log and source
manifest. Access, versions, and API responses can change; a failed source or
hash check should be investigated rather than replaced with fabricated data.
Users must follow each provider's access and use terms when downloading data.
In particular, the [UNCTAD TRAINS terms](https://wits.worldbank.org/data/public/UNCTAD_TermsofUseandDisclaimer.pdf)
govern the tariff source. The package therefore ships neither the raw tariff
records nor the derived design and response data; placing only processed values
in a package would still be a redistribution decision.
For clarity, its tariff request has the form
`https://wits.worldbank.org/API/V1/SDMX/V21/datasource/TRN/reporter/{code}/partner/000/product/all/year/2018/datatype/{reported-or-aveestimated}?format=JSON`;
the script supplies each official reporter code and data type.

## Rebuild and check the inputs

These commands are printed, not evaluated during vignette building. Start in
the `SegreCP` **source directory**, identified by its `DESCRIPTION` file and
`reproducibility/` subdirectory. In the manuscript repository this is
`software/SegreCP`; in a standalone package-source checkout it is the checkout
root. The installed package alone does not contain the download scripts.

You need R >= 4.2 with a working C++ toolchain and the R packages `Rcpp`,
`rTensor`, `data.table`, `digest`, `jsonlite`, and `xml2`. Fresh downloads also
use command-line `bash`, `curl`, and `unzip`. `knitr` is needed only to rebuild
this vignette. These data-preparation scripts expect POSIX absolute paths and
a Unix-like shell (macOS, Linux, or Windows Subsystem for Linux). Choose a
private absolute path **outside** the source checkout;
allow several gigabytes of disk space. The first command downloads data from
the providers and writes to that path, so review their access and use terms
before running it.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# From the SegreCP source directory; edit this private path first.
TRADE_DATA_DIR=/absolute/path/to/private-trade-work
Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("Rcpp", "rTensor", "data.table", "digest", "jsonlite", "xml2"), repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
R CMD INSTALL .
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/run.R \
  --prepare --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR"
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/run.R \
  --check-inputs --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR"
# When only the four processed files remain, this is a weaker, separate check:
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/run.R \
  --check-derived --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR"
```

If all 82 pinned official files are already present under the directory at
their manifest paths, substitute `--prepare --offline` for the online
preparation command. Offline mode validates the files and rebuilds the needed
query metadata locally; it does not call the providers. Use a directory
without the four derived files, because the preparation step refuses to
overwrite them unless explicitly requested.

The four selected derived files live under your private `--data-dir`. The
reader helper below locates their frozen filenames, verifies all four byte
hashes, and aligns their exporter rows:

| Input | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| Response tensor | Exporter keys and 2019 outcomes |
| Design matrix | Six 2018 exporter-level features |
| Fold assignments | Five balanced exporter folds |
| Preprocessing registry | Registered transformations and feature order |

`--check-inputs` verifies all 82 frozen official
sources and the four derived byte hashes, plus keys, dimensions, finite
values, and fold balance. `--check-derived` verifies only the four processed
files; it does **not** establish that the raw data can be downloaded or
reprocessed. `--check-structure` can diagnose structurally valid output after
a provider change, but a structural pass is not an exact frozen-input replay.
None of these checks reruns an optimizer or reproduces the paper's result
table. An interrupted preparation never silently overwrites the four derived
files; see `reproducibility/real_data/README.md` for the explicit recovery
option.

In an isolated offline test, all 82 stored official source files matched their
frozen hashes and rebuilding from them reproduced all four derived files
**byte for byte**. This verifies the recorded source-to-derived workflow from
the pinned files. It does not establish that every provider still serves the
same bytes through a new download, particularly the live WITS API.

## Run the authors' package methods

The source-checkout script `fit_authors_methods.R` fits rank-three RGD and RGN
through `SegreCP::segre_regress()`. It uses the frozen folds and calculates
feature scaling and response centering separately on each training fold. Its
own `--check-inputs` checks the **four processed inputs**, not the 82 raw
sources checked by `run.R --check-inputs`. A one-sweep smoke run checks wiring;
the full five-fold, five-repetition command is the accuracy replay. Both
write outside the package.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# From the SegreCP source directory, with SegreCP installed and the four
# processed files already checked. Edit this path if using a new shell.
TRADE_DATA_DIR=/absolute/path/to/private-trade-work
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/fit_authors_methods.R \
  --check-inputs --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR"
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/fit_authors_methods.R \
  --smoke --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR" \
  --output-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR/authors-smoke"
Rscript reproducibility/real_data/fit_authors_methods.R \
  --folds=1,2,3,4,5 --repetitions=5 --data-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR" \
  --output-dir="$TRADE_DATA_DIR/authors-results"
```

The full run writes `authors_methods_per_fold.csv`,
`authors_methods_summary.csv`, and `authors_methods_objective.csv` to the
chosen output directory, alongside input hashes and the R session record;
smoke files use the `authors_methods_smoke_` prefix. The runner uses the
public package API and explicitly records its settings. On the four
hash-verified processed files, a recorded 50-fit RGD/RGN run matched the
frozen paper rows to numerical precision (largest absolute test-RMSE
difference `9.77e-15`; mean test RMSE 2.7003 for RGD and 2.6684 for RGN).
This **conditional** check does not refit the other five methods or validate
new provider downloads; the separate offline source-to-derived replay is
documented above.
The smoke run only checks execution and dimensions; it is not an accuracy
result.

To visualize empirical convergence after the full run, read the private
objective file. The plot uses the observed training objective, not an
unobservable estimation error or a claim of global convergence.

```{r real-objective-plot, eval=FALSE}
result_dir <- "/absolute/path/to/private-trade-work/authors-results"
trace <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "authors_methods_objective.csv"))
trace <- subset(trace, fold == 1L & repetition == 1L)
rgd <- subset(trace, method == "RGD")
rgn <- subset(trace, method == "RGN")
stopifnot(nrow(rgd) > 0L, nrow(rgn) > 0L,
          all(rgd$objective_ratio > 0), all(rgn$objective_ratio > 0))
plot(rgd$iteration, rgd$objective_ratio, type = "b", log = "y",
     xlab = "Completed sweep", ylab = "Training objective / initial objective",
     col = "#1f77b4", pch = 16)
lines(rgn$iteration, rgn$objective_ratio, type = "b",
      col = "#d95f02", pch = 17)
legend("topright", c("RGD", "RGN"), col = c("#1f77b4", "#d95f02"),
       pch = c(16, 17), lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

## Work with one prepared fold

The next code exposes one fold of the RGN analysis rather than hiding its data
transforms in the runner. It uses the same author-method controls but is **not**
the five-fold, five-repetition paper protocol. Run it from the `SegreCP`
source directory, and set `trade_data_dir` to the private directory used above.
The reader checks the frozen processed inputs before returning aligned `X`,
`Y`, and fold IDs. A rank-three fit on the full response can take substantial
time, so this chunk is not evaluated during package checks.

```{r real-fold, eval=FALSE}
source("reproducibility/real_data/read_prepared_trade_data.R")
trade_data_dir <- "/absolute/path/to/private-trade-work"
trade <- read_prepared_trade_data(trade_data_dir)
X <- trade$X
Y <- trade$Y
fold <- trade$fold
train <- which(fold != 1L)
test <- which(fold == 1L)
x_mean <- colMeans(X[train, , drop = FALSE])
x_sd <- pmax(apply(X[train, , drop = FALSE], 2L, sd), 1e-12)
X_train <- sweep(sweep(X[train, , drop = FALSE], 2L, x_mean),
                 2L, x_sd, "/")
X_test <- sweep(sweep(X[test, , drop = FALSE], 2L, x_mean),
                2L, x_sd, "/")

y_mean <- apply(Y[train, , , , drop = FALSE], 4L, mean)
Y_train <- sweep(Y[train, , , , drop = FALSE], 4L, y_mean)
Y_test <- sweep(Y[test, , , , drop = FALSE], 4L, y_mean)

fit <- SegreCP::segre_regress(
  X_train, Y_train, rank = 3L,
  input_dims = 6L, output_dims = c(25L, 21L, 8L),
  method = "rgn", init = "cpca", init_split = c(1L, 2L),
  design_variance = 1,
  control = SegreCP::segre_control(
    profile = "practical", max_iter = 30L, tolerance = 0,
    step_size = 0.5, step_rule = "backtracking",
    component_order = "decreasing_weight", ridge = 1e-6,
    normalize_regression = "none"
  )
)
prediction <- predict(fit, X_test)
sqrt(mean((as.numeric(prediction) - as.numeric(Y_test))^2))
```

The frozen paper comparison additionally fixes settings and 3/5/10-update
checkpoints for seven methods. The other five estimators are **not exported by
`SegreCP`**; their code belongs to repository-only comparison scripts. The
old seven-method driver also depends on legacy files in the larger manuscript
repository, so there is currently no claim of a standalone seven-method
raw-source-to-table replay from this package checkout. The supported
standalone route here is official-source preparation, input checks, and an
RGD/RGN refit through the package API. The frozen seven-method table recorded
five-fold mean test RMSE of 2.7003 for RGD
and 2.6684 for RGN; these two rows have been independently replayed on the
four hash-verified processed inputs. Wall-clock times are machine-dependent,
so compare methods under one documented timing protocol rather than expecting
identical seconds across computers.

The rebuttal simulation vignettes bundled with the package address different,
synthetic experiments: `rebuttal-regression-reproducibility` and
`rebuttal-initialization-convergence`.

## Minimal installed-package example

This small synthetic example runs during vignette building to check the
tensor-on-tensor input convention without downloading any trade data.

```{r small-api-example}
set.seed(41)
X_demo <- matrix(rnorm(30L * 6L), nrow = 30L)
factors <- lapply(c(6L, 3L, 2L), function(p) {
  z <- rnorm(p)
  z / sqrt(sum(z^2))
})
beta <- array(2 * Reduce(kronecker, rev(factors)), dim = c(6L, 3L, 2L))
Y_demo <- array(as.numeric(X_demo %*% matrix(beta, nrow = 6L)),
                dim = c(30L, 3L, 2L))

demo_fit <- SegreCP::segre_regress(
  X_demo, Y_demo, rank = 1L,
  input_dims = 6L, output_dims = c(3L, 2L),
  method = "rgn", init = "hosvd",
  control = SegreCP::segre_control(max_iter = 2L)
)
dim(predict(demo_fit, X_demo[1:2, , drop = FALSE]))
```
